#en:
I am recording this before I lose the nerve to listen to my own voice.

The bunker is colder than outside. Systems half-dead, dust on every console, like nobody has breathed in here since the last war. I jacked into the relay expecting dead air and junk packets, but the patrol grid was still whispering to itself, looping old atmospheric scans like a nervous habit. Buried in all that static, the same transponder ghost kept reappearing over the border, slipping through restricted airspace and vanishing right over the old barracks line. No alarms, no flags, just quietly filed away and forgotten. Somebody trusted the summaries and never looked at the raw feed again.

I pulled the logs myself, traced the drift pattern, and there it was: a ship riding the same corridor, again and again, like it knew exactly where the blind spot lived. Every course correction points back to those ruined barracks outside Akila, like they are using the ghosts of old casualty reports as cover. Feels like this has been happening for years, hiding in full sight of everyone who stopped paying attention.
zh:
我在自己还没失去勇气听自己声音之前录下这段。

碉堡里比外面还冷。系统半死，每个控制台上都是灰，像自上一场战争以来就没人在这儿呼吸过。我接进中继站时以为只会听到死寂的空气和垃圾数据包，可巡逻网格还在对自己低语，像神经质的习惯一样循环着旧的大气扫描。在那片静电里，同一个应答器幽灵一再出现在边境那边，溜过受限空域，恰好在旧兵营线正上方消失。没有警报，没有标记，只是被悄悄归档、遗忘。有人信任了摘要，再没去看过原始数据流。

我自己调出了日志，追出那漂移图案，它就在那儿：一艘飞船一遍又一遍地走着同一条走廊，像它清楚知道盲区住在哪里。每一次航向修正都指回阿基拉城外那片毁坏的兵营，像他们在用旧伤亡报告的幽灵作掩护。感觉这事已经发生好多年了，堂而皇之地藏在所有不再留意它的人眼皮底下。

#en: Should have burned the cache the first night. It was meant to be a quick skim while the relay was quiet check a few flagged packets, flip them for drink money, forget the rest. Then I saw the pattern tucked under all the spacer noise and Crimson chatter the same correction marks, same timing gaps, slipping through systems that do not share charts. I told myself I would just hold onto one clean slice, something I could trade if the wrong people ever decided I knew too much. That was the oversight. Word got around that I "had Vector on tape." Now I have captains leaning on my door and bounty types sniffing the air like they can smell the bits. I traced one of her cleaner jumps riding a Vanguard transponder they should not have been anywhere near the anomaly she used, but there they were, drive singing almost the same tune as her freelance runs. Whatever she is doing, she has their hardware in her hands, even if they pretend otherwise. From that little corporate lab to this shack, every scrap says the next solid piece of her trail is locked in a dead navy hull that never made it home.
zh: 第一晚就该把那个缓存烧掉的。本来只是想趁中继站安静时快速扫一遍——查几个被标记的数据包，转手换点喝酒的钱，其余的忘掉。可我在所有太空人的噪声和深红舰队的闲聊底下看见了那个图案：同样的修正标记、同样的时序缺口，从互不共享星图的系统之间滑过。我告诉自己，就留一片干净的数据，万一哪天不该知道的人觉得我知道得太多，还能拿去换点什么。那就是我的失手之处。消息传开了，说我"把向量录了下来"。如今有船长堵在我门口，悬赏猎人们像闻得到那些数据似的嗅着空气。我追到她一次比较干净的跃迁：它骑着一个先锋队应答器——那东西本不该靠近她所用的异常区——可它们就在那儿，驱动唱出的调子几乎和她那些自由航次一模一样。不管她在做什么，她手里有他们的硬件，哪怕他们假装没有。从那间小小的企业实验室到这座棚屋，每一块碎片都说，她踪迹的下一块硬料锁在一具再也没能回家的死海军船壳里。

#en:
I did not like coming back to this hole in the rock. The cavern sweats fuel and cold air, and the quartermaster counts crates like they are sins he will never confess. Still, credits loosened his tongue, a little. He never said her name, not once, but his eyes kept flicking to the ceiling, like something could be listening through stone.  

The manifests he finally showed me were scrubbed, but the nav offsets were wrong in a very particular way, a familiar kink in the numbers. Buried in the timing of those jumps is a rendezvous pattern that only resolves if you project it off-world, just above this system's gravity well.  

So the trail now runs: that forgotten outpost where someone left a data crumb, the mismatched docking records tied to a hauler in Neon, and a smuggler here who moved war junk on a schedule that matches neither trade lanes nor patrol sweeps. Three points on a curve that bends up into empty orbit, where someone has been hiding messages in the spaces between official routes, and everyone who has seen it only talks about it in lowered voices, if they talk at all.
zh:
我不喜欢回到这块岩石里的洞。岩洞里渗着燃料和冷气，军需官清点货箱时那副样子，像在数他永远不会忏悔的罪。不过，信用币还是稍微撬开了他的嘴。他从没说过她的名字，一次都没有，可他的眼睛老是瞟向天花板，像有什么东西能透过石头偷听。

他终于给我看的那些清单被擦洗过了，可导航偏移错得很特别，是数字里一种眼熟的扭结。那些跃迁的时序里埋着一个会合图案，只有把它投影到世界之外——就在这个星系重力井的正上方——才解得开。

所以现在这条痕迹是这样走的：那座被人留下一块数据碎屑的被遗忘前哨站、霓虹城一艘货船对不上的停靠记录，以及这里一个走私贩——他运送战争废料的日程既不合贸易航道，也不合巡逻扫描。三点连成一条曲线，向上弯进空荡荡的轨道，那里有人在官方航线之间的空隙里藏消息，而每个见过它的人都只用压低的声音谈论它，如果他们肯谈的话。

#en:
I keep replaying the last clean jump in my head, trying to remember if anything felt wrong. On the scopes it was textbook smooth approach, green lights from the UC tower, a corridor plotted so tight you could shave with it. Nobody questioned it. Why would they We all trust those vectors like gravity.

Then the stories started trickling in, always secondhand. A cousin of a hauler swore a freighter vanished on the same track, but his captain heard it from a GalBank adjuster who blamed pirates. A bartender in New Atlantis told me of a courier that never docked, and she swore she heard it from a Vanguard pilot. Every time I leaned in, they leaned back, said someone else knew more, that they were just passing it along.

Now I am standing on CM-1304, UC crest still stamped over the airlock, and the logs do not match the bodies. The recorded course is pristine, the telemetry too clean, like someone scrubbed out the struggle and left only the math. Whoever laid these lanes knew exactly where they bent, and everyone who ever touched them swears they only heard the warning from someone else.
zh:
我在脑子里一遍遍重放最后那次干净的跃迁，努力回想当时有没有什么地方觉得不对。在示波器上，那是一次教科书般顺畅的进近，联殖塔台亮着绿灯，一条画得紧到你都能拿它刮胡子的走廊。没人质疑它。他们凭什么质疑呢？我们都像信任重力一样信任那些矢量。

然后那些故事开始渗进来，永远是二手的。一个运货船员的表亲赌咒说有一艘货船在同一条轨迹上消失了，可他的船长是从一个把责任推给海盗的银河银行理赔员那儿听来的。新亚特兰蒂斯的一个酒保跟我讲起一艘从未停靠的快船，而她赌咒说是从一名先锋队飞行员那儿听来的。每次我凑近，他们就往后缩，说别人知道得更多，说他们只是把话转手而已。

如今我站在 CM-1304 上，气闸上还盖着联殖的徽记，而日志与尸体对不上。记录的航向完好无损，遥测太干净，像有人把挣扎擦掉，只留下了算式。铺下这些航道的人清楚它们在哪里弯折，而每个碰过它们的人都赌咒说，自己只是从别人那儿听到了那句警告。

#en:
Docking log, personal copy, in case this all disappears like the rest.  

We were only supposed to babysit a drifting support ship for the Trade Authority, run basic checks, sign off on the tow. No one said why the TA tag looked like it had been peeled and re-stuck three times, or why every cargo cradle smelled of burnt lubricant and welding flux. In the cargo spine I found a slab of hull plate with seams too clean for any station yard out here, over-braced like someone expected to take fire. The manifest claimed it was scrap. The crew chief just stared at it, then at me, and changed the subject.  

Funny thing is, a few months back I rotated through an old UC relay where the consoles were full of ghost returns, unregistered work barges popping in and out of junk fields. The tech on duty swore it was sensor drift, then whispered later that the signatures had showed up before, always on routes that suddenly became very profitable for "the right people." Everybody talks like they have it all figured out in the mess, but the moment you suggest putting it in a report, the room goes quiet.
zh:
停靠日志，私人副本，以防这一切像其余东西一样消失。

我们本该只是替贸易管理局照看一艘漂流的支援船，做做基础检查，在拖带上签个字。没人解释为什么那个贸易管理局标签看起来像被撕下来又重新贴了三次，也没人解释为什么每个货架都闻着烧焦的润滑油和焊剂味。在货舱脊里，我找到一块船体装甲板，接缝干净得不像这外面任何一座船坞的手艺，加固得过了头，像有人预料到会挨打。清单说它是废料。船员长只是盯着它，然后盯着我，换了话题。

好笑的是，几个月前我轮换到一座旧联殖中继站，那里的控制台满是幽灵回波，未登记的工作驳船在垃圾场里进进出出。当班的技工赌咒说是传感器漂移，后来又低声说，那些特征以前出现过，总是在那些突然变得对"对的人"非常有利可图的航线上。在食堂里人人都说得头头是道，可你一说要把这写进报告，房间就安静了。

#en:
Dock's quiet now. Just the relay hum and the way the bulkheads creak when the rock flexes. Feels like the whole module is leaning in, listening to see if I talk.

They say this tug pilot never fires a shot. Ships just arrive light, containers written off, everyone shrugs and files the claim. I have seen the gaps behind those shrugs. Partial manifests that do not match hull capacity. Time stamps edited by a shaky hand. Credit transfers routed through dead accounts that somehow still pass Trade Authority checks.

Today a spacer brought me another fragment, said it came off a crate that "never existed." Same route vector I saw on that corrupted record from the research outpost, same ghost ping that bounced off an old relay nobody admits is active. All of it points to the same kind of place: where cargo goes to be forgotten before someone like her makes it useful again.

I am not stupid enough to say the name in the open channel, but I know which depot she has been bleeding dry. Nobody here knows the whole story. We just pass pieces along to people we trust to live long enough to use them.
zh:
码头现在安静了。只有中继站的嗡鸣，以及岩石发生形变时舱壁的吱嘎。感觉整个模块都在往前倾，听着我会不会开口。

他们说这位拖船飞行员从不开一枪。飞船只是轻飘飘地到了，集装箱被注销，人人耸耸肩，把理赔单一交。可我见过那些耸肩背后藏着的窟窿。与船体容量对不上的部分清单。被一只发抖的手改过的时间戳。经由死账户转移、却不知怎的还能通过贸易管理局审查的信用转账。

今天一个太空人又给我带来一块碎片，说是从一只"根本不存在"的货箱上取下的。和我从那座研究前哨站的损坏记录里看到的同一条航路矢量，和从一座没人承认还活着的旧中继站上弹回来的同一个幽灵探测。这一切都指向同一类地方：货物去那里被遗忘，直到像她这样的人让它重新有用。

我还没蠢到在公开频道里说出那个名字，但我知道她一直在把哪座补给站抽干。这里没人掌握完整的故事。我们只是把碎片传给那些我们相信能活够久、用得上它们的人。

#en: I am recording this from the relay bunker, in case someone needs to know why I walked back into a dead grid. The air still smells like old ozone and coolant, like the place is one power spike from remembering it mattered. I pulled the deserter's stolen scans off a buried buffer, the ones no one filed because they were easier to ignore than explain. Same patrol, same sweep pattern, but there is a shadow in the upper atmosphere that does not match any registered transponder, holding position right above that forgotten station on the ridge. It is all there in the timestamps and angles; you can almost feel the course corrections, like someone threading a needle through a gap the charts say does not exist. Maybe it is safer for everyone if that kind of flying stays a rumor, but pretending we never saw it is how we got here in the first place. The last listening post gave us ghost readings that did not line up with the public lanes, the deserter confirmed a ship cutting through restricted sky on a path nobody admits is real, and now the numbers point straight back to that same quiet station, waiting.
zh: 我在中继碉堡里录下这段，以防有人需要知道我为什么走回一张死电网。空气里还是旧臭氧和冷却液的味道，像这地方只差一次电力尖峰就会想起自己曾经重要过。我从一个埋起来的缓冲区里调出那名逃兵偷来的扫描记录——那些没人归档的，因为忽略它们比解释它们更省事。同样的巡逻，同样的扫描图案，可上层大气里有一道与任何登记应答器都不匹配的暗影，就悬在山脊上那座被遗忘的空间站正上方。一切都写在时间戳和角度里；你几乎能感觉到那些航向修正，像有人把线穿过一道星图声称不存在的缝隙。也许让那种飞行保持为传言，对所有人都更安全，可假装我们从没见过它，正是我们走到今天这步的原因。上一座监听站给了我们对不上公开航道的幽灵读数，那名逃兵证实了一艘飞船沿着没人承认真实的路径切开受限天空，而现在数字笔直地指回那座同样安静的空间站，等着。

#en: I keep replaying the last jump profile in my head, like if I stare at the numbers long enough they will admit what we all refuse to say out loud. The Trustsphere should not be here, cold and torn open on a lane that was sold to us as safer than dockside. I walked past a hundred holo-ads in New Atlantis promising that GalBank watches over its investments like family; funny how none of those clips show a vault deck vented to vacuum. The nav buffers are scarred with corrections that are too elegant to be accidents, little nudges lining us up with someone's private kill box. When I took this side contract out of that busted quarter on Akila, it was supposed to be a clean audit, a chance to prove to my old crew I still had a future. I tagged the corrupted chains, flagged the inconsistencies, left a note to myself that I would come back with proper tools and a clearer head. I never did. If anyone finds this, know that the pattern started with a cheap dataslate in the dirt and angry spacers muttering about discount routes; it led here, to a dead protection ship that proves the odds were never on our side.
zh: 我在脑子里一遍遍重放最后那次跃迁剖面，像只要盯着那些数字看得够久，它们就会承认我们都不肯说出口的事。信托球号不该在这里，冰冷、被撕开，躺在那条被卖给我们时说比码头边还安全的航道上。我在新亚特兰蒂斯走过上百个全息广告，保证银河银行像照顾家人一样照看它的投资；好笑的是，那些片子没有一个拍的是被抽成真空的金库甲板。导航缓冲里满是疤痕般的修正，优雅得不像意外，一点点轻推把我们送进某人的私人杀伤区。当初我从阿基拉那片破败街区接下这份私活时，它本该是一次干净的审计，一个向老船员证明我仍有前途的机会。我标记了那些损坏的链条，标出了出入之处，给自己留了张便条，说我会带着正规工具和更清醒的头脑回来。我从没做到。要是有人找到这段，请知道这个图案始于泥土里一块廉价数据板和一群怒骂折扣航线的太空人；它把我引到这里，一艘死去的保护船，证明胜算从来不在我们这边。

#en: I thought this would be another dead end like the rest of my assignments out here, one more "monitor and report" buried under nicer words. The outpost is barely more than a sealed room, a crackling comm dish, and a bunk that smells like whoever had it before me smoked in their sleep. Still, the relay hears everything the lanes whisper past. Today, buried inside routine telemetry and a half-corrupted freighter ping, I caught it again: that same fractional drift in the jump solutions, the same signature from a skiff we lost six months back when Command told me my timestamps were off. I only saw it because Ops sent the wrong filter profile, the deck tech typoed a ship ID, and I forgot to purge yesterday's buffer. A chain of small mistakes no one will ever admit. Crossed with that old LIST incident file I was told to "deprioritize," it all folds toward a scrapyard orbiting Deimos that somehow features in traffic patterns way above its importance. So far I have a trail of dismissed reports, an anonymous tip from a nervous hauler, and now a set of lane deviations all curving toward the same patch of rust.
zh: 我以为这会像我这外面其余的任务一样，又是一条死胡同，又一次被更漂亮的措辞包装起来的"监控并报告"。那座前哨站不过是一间密封的房间、一只噼啪作响的通讯天线，还有一张散发着上任睡梦中抽烟味道的铺位。不过，凡是从航道上低语而过的东西，中继站都听得见。今天，在例行遥测和一个损坏了一半的货船探测里，我又逮到了它：跃迁解算里同样那点分数级的漂移，和六个月前我们损失的那艘小艇一样的特征——当时指挥部还告诉我是我的时间戳不准。我能看到它，只是因为作战部发错了过滤配置文件、甲板技工打错了一个船号，而我又忘了清空昨天的缓冲区。一连串没人会承认的小错误。把它和我被要求"降低优先级"的那份独立盟旧事件档案交叉比对，一切都朝着一座绕火卫二运转的废料场折过去——那地方不知怎的出现在远高于它重要性的交通图案里。到现在为止，我有一条被驳回的报告线、一条来自紧张运货船员的匿名线索，以及现在这一组全都朝同一片锈迹弯曲的航道偏移。

#en:
I keep thinking if I say this out loud, it becomes real, so here it goes.

I ran manifests for a hauler out past New Atlantis, thought I knew how the numbers were supposed to look. Then we picked up that stray slate in the drift, all mismatched dates and dead transponders, pointing back to Trade Authority traffic it had no business knowing about. I laughed it off until I checked a personal account and half my life was suddenly "under review."

By the time I reached the city branch, the clerk downstairs swore my file had always been like that. Same tone at every window, the same little pauses when they read my name. Even the lawyer I found in the lower levels said there had been "another version" of my case once, but whatever it was got folded into rumor and bar talk a long time ago. Now I am sitting in the dark of this support ship, listening to its cooling metal, and the shape of it all is starting to show; quiet edits in station ledgers, cargo that moved without moving, and a whisper that the first person who tried to explain it disappeared from the records before anyone wrote down what they saw.
zh:
我一直觉得要是把这话大声说出来，它就会成真，所以——说来就来吧。

我曾为新亚特兰蒂斯外面一艘货船跑清单，以为自己知道那些数字该是什么样。后来我们在漂移带里捡到那块游离的数据板，日期全都对不上，应答器全死了，却指向它本没资格知道的贸易管理局交通。我一笑置之，直到我查了一个个人账户，我半辈子忽然"处于审查中"。

等我赶到城里那个分行时，楼下的文员赌咒说我的档案一直就是那样。每个窗口都用同样的语气，念到我名字时都有同样的小停顿。连我在下层找到的律师都说，我的案子曾经有过"另一个版本"，可不管它是什么，很久以前就被揉进传言和酒吧闲谈里了。如今我坐在这艘支援船的黑暗里，听着它冷却的金属，整件事的轮廓开始显现：站点账簿里安静的改动、没动却移动了的货物，以及一句低语——第一个试图解释它的人，在有人写下所见之前，就已经从记录里消失了。
